parts.text: A student investigates resistance. Refer to Figure 2.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Figure 2.2 shows the readings on the meters.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Record the current I 1 shown in Figure 2.2. Include the unit. I 1 = .................................. unit ............... [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Record the potential difference (p.d.) V 1 across the resistance wire BC shown in Figure 2.2. Include the unit. V 1 = .................................. unit ............... [2]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the resistance R 1 of the resistance wire using the equation: R 1 = V 1 I 1 . R 1 = ...................................................... Ω [1]

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) The length of the resistance wire is 50 cm. Calculate r, the resistance per cm of the resistance wire, using the equation: r = R 1 50 cm . r = ............................................... Ω / cm [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student has a length of the same resistance wire wound on a wooden rod, as shown in Figure 2.3.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Record the number of whole turns N of wire on the rod. N = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The student measures the diameter d of the rod. d = ............................................................... Calculate a value l 1 for the length of wire on the rod using the equation: l 1 = Nπd. l 1 = .................................................... cm [1] 2.3 cm

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student: • disconnects the resistance wire from the circuit shown in Figure 2.1 • connects the wire on the rod to the circuit at B and C • measures the current I 2 in the circuit I 2 = ............................................................... • measures the potential difference (p.d.) V 2 across the resistance wire on the rod. V 2 = ............................................................... 0.41 A 1.8 V

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate the resistance R 2 of the resistance wire on the rod using the equation: R 2 = V 2 I 2 . R 2 = ...................................................... Ω [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate another value l 2 for the length of resistance wire on the rod using your values from 2(a)(iv) and 2(c)(i) and the equation: l 2 = R 2 r . Give your answer in centimetres to the nearest millimetre. l 2 = .................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 2(c)(ii)
ms.text: l2 calculated and to nearest mm

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:

Sensible comparison with other method
